Old Timey Code

Old Timey Code

send(to, from, count)
register short *to, *from;
register count;
{
        register n=(count+7)/8;
        switch(count%8){
        case 0: do{     *to = *from++;
        case 7:         *to = *from++;
        case 6:         *to = *from++;
        case 5:         *to = *from++;
        case 4:         *to = *from++;
        case 3:         *to = *from++;
        case 2:         *to = *from++;
        case 1:         *to = *from++;
                }while(--n>0);
        }
}
float Q_rsqrt(float number) {
     long i;
     float x2, y;
     const float threehalfs = 1.5F;

     x2 = number * 0.5F;
     y  = number;
     i  = *(long*)&y;                             // evil floating point bit level hacking
     i  = 0x5f3759df - ( i >> 1 );                // what the heck?
     y  = *(float*)&i;
     y  = y * ( threehalfs - ( x2 * y * y ) );    // 1st iteration
     // y  = y * ( threehalfs - ( x2 * y * y ) ); // 2nd iteration, this can be removed

     return y;
}

Old Timey Code vs. Mono 

0123456789aces.,:;‘’“”=()[]{}`~
0123456789aces.,:;‘’“”=()[]{}`~
0123456789aces.,:;‘’“”=`~()[]{}
0123456789aces.,:;‘’“”=`~()[]{}

Old Timey Mono is a best-effort faithful revival of Reproducing Typewriter. Old Timey Code alters some glyphs to make it more usable for coding. Note the digits zero and one, the more open arpetures in the letters “aces”, the larger punctuation marks, equal sign, brackets, backtick, and tilde.
